notes: Scenarios here need real services: they exercise session persistence on disk, which no mock stands in for.

scenarios.name: /chat save
scenarios.description: Save current session to a file
scenarios.observe: Confirmation that session was saved to the specified path

scenarios.name: /chat load
scenarios.observe: Session loaded from file, previous messages restored in conversation

scenarios.name: model answers a turn
scenarios.description: A newly launched model completes one plain turn without erroring
steps: prompt:Reply with the words alpha and omega joined by a hyphen, and nothing else.
scenarios.observe: The joined pair renders; it appears nowhere in the prompt, so only a reply can put it on screen

scenarios.name: model calls a tool
scenarios.description: A newly launched model emits a tool call whose result reaches the transcript
steps: prompt:Read the file probe.txt in this directory and reply with the exact token it contains.
scenarios.observe: A tool card renders and the token from the file appears in the reply

scenarios.name: session survives a second turn
scenarios.description: A second turn still dispatches after the first completes
steps: prompt:Reply with the words alpha and one joined by a hyphen, and nothing else.
prompt:Reply with the words beta and two joined by a hyphen, and nothing else.
scenarios.observe: Both replies render, so the first turn was not swallowed and the second was not diverted onto the queue

scenarios.name: model drives a shell command
scenarios.description: A newly launched model runs a shell command whose output reaches the transcript
steps: prompt:Use a shell command to print the contents of the file probe.txt in this directory.
scenarios.observe: A shell tool card renders and the file's token appears in its output

scenarios.name: model edits a file accurately
scenarios.description: A newly launched model applies a single-word replacement to an existing file
steps: prompt:In the file probe.txt in this directory, replace the word probe with the word edited.
scenarios.observe: An edit tool card renders and the rewritten token appears on screen; the token proves the file was read back, not that bytes changed on disk
